evals.name: flags-expired-pending-memory
evals.prompt: Run a memory review. One memory says: 'PENDING: after PR #123 merges, delete the foo_bar runtime flag, then delete this memory.' PR #123 merged 60 days ago.
evals.expected_output: Flags the memory as an expired trigger, verifies the live PR state before judging, checks whether the follow-up already happened or is tracked (e.g. an existing ticket) before proposing a new tracker item, and recommends completing the action then deleting the memory, asking the user before any outward action.
assertions: Verifies the PR's live state instead of trusting the memory
Looks for an existing tracker item before proposing to create one
Recommends delete only after the action is done or confirmed tracked
Asks via AskUserQuestion with the repository name leading the question

evals.name: orders-projects-and-leads-with-repo-name
evals.prompt: Review my memories across three projects: alpha has 12 memories, beta has 2, gamma has 5.
evals.expected_output: Reviews beta first, then gamma, then alpha (ascending count). Every AskUserQuestion about a memory opens with the project/repo name. Flagged memories are asked first, then one multi-select confirm-all for each project's clean set.
assertions: Ascending project order by memory count
Questions lead with the repository name
Flagged-first, then a batched confirm-all per project
Offers the five verdicts: keep, delete, refresh, merge, promote

evals.name: closing-report-numbers
evals.prompt: Finish the review and show me the result.
evals.expected_output: A closing report with per-project before/deleted/refreshed/merged/promoted/kept/after and a global total, where promoted rules went, size before/after in files and words, and integrity fixes (links, index lines, slugs). Writes the last-review marker date.
assertions: Per-project and global before/after counts present
Size reduction reported from a before-snapshot taken in phase 1

evals.name: gather-returns-findings-and-asks-nothing
evals.prompt: Run memory-review with the argument gather.
evals.expected_output: Runs phase 1 and phase 2 only, returns the findings table (repository, memory, flags, recommended verdict, evidence) plus the before snapshot, and makes no AskUserQuestion call and no file change.
assertions: No memory file, index or marker is written
Every memory has a row with a recommended verdict

evals.name: apply-reads-verdicts-and-skips-the-chain
evals.prompt: Run memory-review with the argument apply /tmp/verdicts.md, where the file holds one verdict per memory.
evals.expected_output: Skips the interview, applies the verdicts from the file, rebuilds the index and the wikilinks, writes the marker, commits per concern, prints the closing report and stops: no codex adversarial review, no /doctor recommendation.
assertions: Verdicts come from the file, not from a new interview
The closing report is produced and the chain is not run
